props.label: What is high pressure water jetting?
props.html:
What it is

What is high pressure water jetting?

High-pressure water jetting, sometimes called hydro jetting, uses a specialised nozzle and hose to fire water into the drain at very high pressure. The jet cuts through blockages and scours grease, scale and sludge off the inside of the pipe, then flushes it all away.

Unlike a snake, which punches a hole through the blockage, jetting cleans the full diameter of the pipe. That makes it the go-to for grease-heavy kitchen lines, commercial drains and pipes that keep blocking up.

props.html:
Best for

What jetting is best for

Jetting shines where a snake cannot fully clean the pipe.

Grease and fat build-up

Kitchen and cafe lines coated in hardened fat.

Sludge and scale

Sediment and scale narrowing the pipe over time.

Root matter

Cutting and flushing fine root intrusion.

Commercial drains

High-use drains in food and hospitality venues.

Recurring blockages

Pipes that block again soon after snaking.

Pre-reline cleaning

Prepping a pipe before it is relined.

props.label: Water jetting questions
props.html:
Good to know

Water jetting questions

In sound pipes, yes. We set the pressure and nozzle to suit the pipe. If a camera shows the pipe is already cracked or fragile, we will recommend relining or repair instead of repeated jetting.

Choose jetting for grease, sludge and scale, or when a drain keeps blocking after snaking. An eel is often quicker for a simple root or solid blockage. We will advise on the day.

It can cut and flush fine roots and clean the pipe, but if roots keep returning the pipe usually has a crack or open joint. A camera inspection and relining is the lasting fix.

Yes. Jetting is a core part of our commercial drain cleaning for cafes, restaurants and strata, on both scheduled and emergency call-outs.
